title: GLT identity makes the anomaly defect LITERALLY the Hasse-Weil Betti error
evidence: Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C010_glt_betti.py + inline checks, exact integer (FFT over Z/p) point counts at PROPER-SUBGROUP primes (dyadic mu_n, n^2<<q, beta=3..4.5; n=8,16,32). PROVEN HALF: (S1) the r=2 closed form V4 = sum_s eta_s^4 = 3p(n-1)-n^3 holds EXACTLY (diff 0) at every prize-regime prime tested (n=8 p=521,1481,4129,11593; n=16 p=4129..262193; n=32 p=32801..5931649) -- it is LINEAR in p with NO sqrt(p) term, so the r=2 Hasse-Weil error term vanishes identically. (S2) The full GLT moment<->variety IDENTITY holds exactly: V_k(over m coset reps) = (p*M_k - n^k)/n where M_k = #{(x_1..x_k) in mu_n^k : sum x_i = 0} is the subgroup-diagonal (modified-Fermat) point count -- verified match=True for all r=2,3,4 at n=8,16 (e.g. n=16 p=257 r=4: V_8=56044777 = (257*20201104-16^8)/16). So 'E_r IS exactly a hypersurface point count' is a genuine exact identity. REFUTED HALF: (a) the 'anomaly defect E_r - E_r^C IS the Hasse-Weil error' claim -- the measured defect V_k - (2r-1)!! m n^r is NEGATIVE (deficit, ratio V_k/ceil = 0.87,0.94,0.97 at r=2 for n=8,16,32) and SHRINKS toward 1 as n grows (finite-n CLT-toward-Gaussian artifact), not a genus-growing fixed Betti error. (b) the crossover claim is quantitatively wrong: with C010's OWN formulas, the crude Betti scale m^{2r-1}*sqrt(p) overtakes the diagonal (2r-1)!! n^r m ALREADY AT r=2 (r_cross=2 for all prize n=256..2^30, beta=4,5), NOT 'at r>=3 at a crossover = r_max=2 log_n p = 8..10'. At r=2 the TRUE error is 0 while m^3 sqrt(p) ~ 1.76e13 (n=16 p=65537) -- so m^{2r-1} is NOT the genuine primitive Betti number and the r_max/cumulant-onset matching is built on a wrong Betti estimate.
honest_note: The GLT identity itself (period moment = exact modified-Fermat/subgroup-diagonal point count) is real, classical, and exactly verified in the prize regime -- a legitimate and useful structural fact (forms F5/F12/F13). What is NOT established is the operative C010 claim that the char-p defect EQUALS a specific Hasse-Weil error term and that a Betti/genus bound therefore pins the deep-moment wall at r_max. The measured defect is a negative finite-n deficit, not a genus-growing error; the crude m^{2r-1} Betti estimate is off (overshoots at r=2 where the true error is 0). The genuine open core -- BGK sqrt-cancellation among the m Gauss-period phases chi-bar(b)tau(chi), |tau|=sqrt(p) -- is NOT reduced to a clean Hasse-Weil/genus bound by this identity; bounding the actual (small, sub-Gaussian) error of the modified-Fermat variety in the n=2^mu prize regime IS the same open Paley/BGK/W-Betti wall. So W-anomaly and W-Betti are not collapsed by an *exact* equation beyond the trivial 'point count = main + error'. Refuted numerics (defect sign, r_cross=2) should be logged in DISPROOF_LOG.md.
reduced_to: Prove a genuine Hasse-Weil/genus bound on the TRUE error of the modified-Fermat subgroup-diagonal variety {sum x_i^n = 0} cap mu_n^{2r} at r ~ 2 log_n p in the proper-subgroup regime n=2^mu, n^2 << q -- i.e. show the (negative, sub-Gaussian) defect V_k - (2r-1)!! m n^r is O(genus * sqrt(p)) with genus the ACTUAL primitive Betti number (not the crude m^{2r-1}). This is the same object as the BGK/Paley char-sum bound, restated geometrically.
wall: W-Betti / W-anomaly (= BGK sqrt-cancellation / Paley Graph Conjecture for thin mu_n); the identity is genuine but the error bound is the unchanged open core.
